messages.subject: Asymmetric violin plots
parts: Is there an easy way of creating violin plots with the left part and the right par coming from data from 2 different groups? Population pyramid which do age distribution for males to the left and females to the right would be role model.

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: Asymmetric violin plots
parts:
Violin plots use geom_polygon to do the drawing, after doing a
stat_density on the data. So assuming you have df$x, y1, and y2, I'd
try these steps:

1) call d1 <- density(df$y1) and d2 <- density(df$y1) to get the
respective distributions
2) create data frame newdata1 <- data.frame(x=df$x + d1$y *
some_scaling_factor, y=d1$x)
3) create data frame newdata2 <- data.frame(x=df$x - d1$y *
some_scaling_factor, y=d1$x)
4) sort the points in each data frame, one ascending by y, other
descending, so it will draw correctly
5) rbind these data together
6) close the polygon: add a final point that's same as the first one
7) call geom_polygon to draw it

Note - I haven't tried this, but seems like it should produce what you want.

Ben
